source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:6 ('רקיע — the Michlol: as the breath-letters sound though unwritten, so a STOLEN letter is read before a final guttural — we say the firmament-word as if an aleph slipped in before the ayin, though none is written')
claim_en: THE STOLEN LETTER'S WRITTEN TRACE: רקיע ('let there be a FIRMAMENT,' 1:6) ends in a guttural that the mouth reaches through an unwritten glide — the Michlol's 'stolen letter,' sounded but never written. The stream carries the rule's one visible trace: the patach written directly on the final ayin, out of the letter-then-vowel order every other vowel keeps (DB-checked) — the pointing system's own mark for the sound that has no letter.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 1:7 ('מעל לרקיע — two in the Masorah: here, and A VOICE FROM ABOVE THE FIRMAMENT in Ezekiel's chariot: as the work of creation is not expounded in public, so the work of the chariot')
claim_en: ABOVE THE FIRMAMENT, TWICE: the phrase מעל לרקיע ('the waters ABOVE THE FIRMAMENT,' 1:7) stands exactly once in the Torah (DB-checked); its one Scripture partner is the voice from above the firmament of Ezekiel's chariot-vision (1:25, named) — the Kitzur binding the two guarded teachings, creation and the chariot, by the two phrases that reach above the sky.
